item.text:
Research continuation completed for all eight selected chapters. No scores assigned.

The environment still blocks filesystem access, so `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be updated. New units are ready for ingestion; existing methodology mappings should remain unchanged.

New defensible units:

- `WEB-1B-022` — AU/COMESA observers documented that Egypt’s 10–12 December 2023 election was administered by the legally established National Election Authority and involved 70 observers from 36 African states. This supports formal administration, but not competitive fairness. Maps to `1B.2`, `1B.10`. [AU/COMESA statement](https://au.int/sites/default/files/pressreleases/43407-pr-Preliminary_Statement_-AUEOM_in_Egypt_-_Dec_2023_ENG1.pdf), pp. 1–2, lines 10–30.

- `WEB-2B-009` — Reuters reported that aid was delayed in October 2023, with hundreds of tonnes stuck at El-Arish, while Egypt and Israel disputed responsibility for Rafah’s impaired operation. This independently qualifies the humanitarian-facilitation record: Egypt enabled a corridor, but access was constrained and responsibility was shared. Maps to `2B.4`, `2B.6`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/gaza-aid-stuck-as-egypt-says-israel-not-cooperating-3199548), lines 421–455.

- `WEB-2B-010` — The ICRC described Egypt as a hub for humanitarian operations concerning Gaza and Sudan and reported coordination with the Egyptian Red Crescent during 2023. This independently corroborates Egypt’s facilitation role without establishing diplomatic effectiveness. Maps to `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [ICRC 2023 factsheet](https://www.icrc.org/en/document/icrc-activites-egypt-facts-figures-2023), lines 172–187.

- `WEB-3B-006` — The UN Committee against Torture’s 2023 process and Egypt’s submitted responses provide a primary institutional record for testing allegations of torture, unlawful detention, and disciplinary action. The material reports Egyptian claims of legal and disciplinary measures but does not independently establish that remedies were effective. Maps to `3B.1`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.9`. [UN CAT record](https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/4026755/files/CAT_C_EGY_RQ_5-EN.pdf).

- `WEB-4B-011` — The opened AU/COMESA statement confirms the election’s dates, formal election authority, international observation mission, and normative democratic standards. It supplies a precise primary locator for the previously snippet-only observer evidence; further pages should be retained for the mission’s substantive findings. Maps to `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [AU/COMESA statement](https://au.int/sites/default/files/pressreleases/43407-pr-Preliminary_Statement_-_AUEOM_in_Egypt_-_Dec_2023_ENG1.pdf), lines 2–30.

- `WEB-5B-009` — The World Bank’s 2023–2027 Egypt partnership framework identifies private-sector jobs, improved health and education, social protection, macroeconomic resilience, governance, and citizen engagement as stated development objectives. This is evidence of an externally documented policy framework, not proof of delivery. Maps to `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`. [World Bank CPF](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/factsheet/2023/03/21/egypt-country-partnership-framework-fy2023-2027).

- `WEB-6B-006` — The World Bank reports that by December 2023 Takaful and Karama covered 4.67 million households, with approximately 17 million people enrolled; it also reports strong targeting performance and independent evaluations showing gains in consumption, school enrollment, nutrition, and poverty avoidance. This is the strongest new favorable implementation/outcome unit for social protection, though several evaluations predate 2023. Maps to `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`, `6B.7`, `6B.9`, `6B.10`. [World Bank results report](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs), lines 69–78.

- `WEB-6B-007` — The WHO–World Bank 2023 UHC monitoring release reports global stagnation in health-service coverage and severe financial hardship from out-of-pocket payments, providing an independent adverse benchmark for assessing Egypt’s incomplete health-insurance rollout. It is not Egypt-specific, so it should be used only as contextual calibration, not as a country outcome. Maps to `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`. [WHO/World Bank UHC report](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/09/18/billions-left-behind-on-the-path-to-universal-health-coverage), lines 103–123.

- `WEB-7B-006` — AP reported that former anti-corruption chief Hesham Genena was released in February 2023 after serving a five-year sentence related to criticism of the military and corruption allegations. The account records a direct personal nexus between the presidency, an anti-corruption watchdog, and punishment of its former head, but does not prove the underlying corruption allegations. Maps to `7B.2`, `7B.6`, `7B.7`, `7B.9`. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/politics-egypt-government-cairo-471b32e0f7edcfdc9664179c8e32ec00), lines 1745–1760.

- `WEB-8B-006` — The World Bank’s Takaful/Karama record shows concrete 2023 delivery: coverage rose to almost five million households and benefit levels increased by 40 percent, while the system used a shock-responsive social registry. This provides specific implementation evidence for competence in one sector, while leaving broader cross-sector effectiveness unresolved. Maps to `8B.2`, `8B.4`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs), lines 73–89.

Disposition correction:

- `WEB-1B-006` remains rejected for evidentiary use because its supplied publication date is future-dated. Retain the Russian fuel/storage dependence only as a research lead pending a contemporaneous contract or Rosatom/NPPA source.

Chapter outcome:

- `1B`: formal nuclear safeguards, emergency planning, and cyber-governance structures improved; independent operational safety and incident evidence remain unavailable.
- `2B`: humanitarian facilitation is independently corroborated, but access was materially constrained and mediation effectiveness remains unresolved.
- `3B`: primary UN process material was recovered, but remedy effectiveness remains unproven.
- `4B`: AU/COMESA election evidence is now opened and precisely located; substantive observer findings still require extraction.
- `5B`: policy-framework evidence improved, but target-year household and labor outcomes remain limited.
- `6B`: strong new favorable evidence supports Takaful/Karama coverage and measured benefits; health and education outcomes remain incomplete.
- `7B`: the Genena record supplies a direct integrity/accountability nexus, but not personal enrichment or corruption proof against Sisi.
- `8B`: sector-specific delivery evidence improved through Takaful/Karama; broad administrative competence and durable outcomes remain mixed.

No chapter is fully closed, but the recoverable review tasks were attempted across the complete selected scope.
